title: Subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis: low radioactive iodine uptake
vignette: A 25-year-old woman comes to the office due to a 2-week history of neck pain. The patient had an upper respiratory infection a month ago, during which she experienced nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and a cough productive of clear sputum; her respiratory symptoms lasted for 5 days and resolved spontaneously. The patient then felt well until 2 weeks ago, when she developed pain in the anterior neck associated with mild fever, palpitations, and excessive sweating. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. Pulse is 110/min. The thyroid gland is tender to palpation and diffusely enlarged. Other findings include sweaty palms, fine hand tremor, and brisk deep tendon reflexes. Laboratory studies show suppressed TSH and elevated free thyroxine levels. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 70 mm/hr. Which of the following additional findings is most likely to be present in this patient at this time?

clues.text: upper respiratory infection a month ago
clues.note: A preceding viral illness is the classic trigger for subacute (granulomatous, de Quervain) thyroiditis.
A PAINFUL, tender thyroid is the hallmark that distinguishes subacute thyroiditis from painless/autoimmune causes of hyperthyroidism.

clues.text: thyroid gland is tender to palpation and diffusely enlarged
clues.note: A tender, diffusely enlarged goiter with hyperthyroid symptoms after a viral illness is characteristic of subacute thyroiditis.

clues.text: suppressed TSH and elevated free thyroxine
clues.note: Biochemical hyperthyroidism (low TSH, high free T4) in this setting is due to RELEASE of preformed hormone from destroyed follicles, not new synthesis.
A markedly elevated ESR reflects the inflammatory (granulomatous) nature of subacute thyroiditis.

whatMatters: Painful, tender goiter after a viral illness + hyperthyroidism (low TSH, high free T4) + high ESR = SUBACUTE (granulomatous, de Quervain) THYROIDITIS. Because inflammation DESTROYS follicles and releases PREFORMED hormone (no new synthesis), thyroid metabolic activity/iodine trapping is low -> LOW RADIOACTIVE IODINE UPTAKE. Answer B.
strategy: Distinguish thyroiditis (destruction-release) from Graves (overproduction) by radioiodine uptake: subacute thyroiditis = LOW uptake (gland not synthesizing/trapping iodine); Graves = HIGH, diffuse uptake. The painful tender gland + high ESR + preceding virus = subacute thyroiditis -> LOW uptake. Reject elevated TPO antibodies (Hashimoto/Graves autoimmune, typically painless), low thyroglobulin (thyroglobulin is HIGH from follicular destruction), and low T3 (T3 is elevated in hyperthyroidism).

eliminations.label: Elevated TPO antibodies - autoimmune (painless) thyroid disease (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: thyroid peroxidase antibodies mark AUTOIMMUNE thyroid disease (Hashimoto, Graves). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: subacute thyroiditis is a POST-VIRAL, PAINFUL, inflammatory process (not primarily autoimmune); the painful tender gland + high ESR point to it, and TPO antibodies are usually not the defining feature. ✅ Correct if: painless autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto).

eliminations.label: Low serum thyroglobulin - it's HIGH from destruction
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: thyroglobulin, released when thyroid follicles break down. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: follicular destruction in subacute thyroiditis RELEASES thyroglobulin, so it is ELEVATED, not low. ✅ Correct if: exogenous thyroid hormone intake (factitious - low thyroglobulin).

eliminations.label: Low serum triiodothyronine - T3 is elevated
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: serum T3. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: in the hyperthyroid phase, released preformed hormone RAISES both T4 and T3; T3 is not low. ✅ Correct if: euthyroid sick syndrome (low T3) in severe illness.

reasoning: Painful, tender goiter after a viral URI + hyperthyroid labs + high ESR = subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis
Inflammation destroys follicles and releases PREFORMED hormone (no new synthesis)
With no active hormone synthesis, the gland traps little iodine -> low radioactive iodine uptake
-> low radioactive iodine uptake; answer B
mechanism: Subacute (granulomatous, de Quervain) thyroiditis characteristically follows a VIRAL upper respiratory infection and is thought to result from a cross-reacting inflammatory response with cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-mediated destruction of thyroid follicles. Clinically it produces a PAINFUL, tender, diffusely enlarged thyroid, fever, and an elevated ESR. Follicular destruction RELEASES stored, preformed thyroid hormone, causing an initial HYPERTHYROID phase (suppressed TSH, elevated free T4/T3, elevated thyroglobulin) with adrenergic symptoms. Crucially, because the gland is being destroyed rather than overproducing hormone, it is NOT actively synthesizing hormone or trapping iodine - so RADIOACTIVE IODINE UPTAKE is LOW (versus the HIGH, diffuse uptake of Graves disease, which is driven by TSH-receptor-stimulating antibodies). After the stored hormone is depleted, patients pass through a transient HYPOthyroid phase and then usually return to euthyroid. Management is supportive (NSAIDs, beta blockers; steroids if severe). The distractors are wrong because thyroglobulin is elevated (not low), T3 is elevated (not low), and TPO antibodies characterize painless autoimmune disease rather than this painful post-viral thyroiditis.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Endo > subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis: post-viral, PAINFUL tender goiter, high ESR; hyperthyroid phase from hormone release -> LOW radioiodine uptake; self-limited (hyper -> hypo -> euthyroid).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Destruction releases preformed hormone, so uptake is LOW (contrast Graves = high uptake).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on radioactive iodine uptake, subacute/de Quervain thyroiditis, thyroglobulin, or destructive vs synthetic hyperthyroidism? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: TPO antibodies = autoimmune/painless; thyroglobulin is HIGH (destruction); T3 is elevated in hyperthyroidism.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: subacute thyroiditis = painful goiter + high ESR + LOW radioiodine uptake (destruction-release); Graves = high uptake.

keywords.front: Painful tender goiter after a viral URI + high ESR + hyperthyroid

keywords.back: LOW (hormone released from destruction, no synthesis)

firstAid.detail: Endo: painful goiter, high ESR, hyperthyroid phase; LOW radioiodine uptake (destruction).
Endo > Graves (high uptake, TSH-R Ab), Hashimoto (TPO Ab, painless), thyroglobulin high in destruction.
Endo > transient hyper -> hypo -> euthyroid; self-limited.

memoryHook: A sore, post-viral thyroid dumps its stored hormone and then goes quiet - it's not making hormone, so radioiodine uptake is LOW (the opposite of Graves).
